title.zh: 卷388 列傳一百七十五 桂良 瑞麟子：怀塔布 官文 文煜
title.en: Volume 388 Biographies 175: Gui Liang, Rui Lin son: Huai Tabu, Guan Wen, Wen Yu
title.raw: 卷388 列傳一百七十五 桂良 瑞麟子：怀塔布 官文 文煜

sentences.zh: 桂良，字燕山，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正紅旗人，閩浙總督玉德子。

translations.literal: Gui Liang, courtesy name Yanshan, of the Guwalgiya clan, a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner, was the son of Yude, governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Liang, styled Yanshan, belonged to the Guwalgiya clan and the Manchu Plain Red Banner; he was the son of Yude, governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 入貲為禮部主事，晉員外郎。

translations.literal: He purchased entry and became a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites, then was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He gained office by purchase as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites and was later promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 出為四川順慶知府，調成都。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as prefect of Shunqing in Sichuan, then was transferred to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as prefect of Shunqing in Sichuan, then transferred to the Chengdu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷建昌道，河南按察使，四川、廣東、江西布政使。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Jianchang circuit intendant, Henan provincial judicial commissioner, and provincial treasurer of Sichuan, Guangdong, and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Jianchang circuit intendant, Henan judicial commissioner, and treasurer of Sichuan, Guangdong, and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 道光十四年，擢河南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of the Daoguang reign, he was promoted to governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 14 (1834), he was appointed governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，林清、李文成等以八卦教倡亂，既誅，而汲縣潞州屯墳塔猶祀其神曰「無生老母」，習教者猶眾。

translations.literal: In the Jiaqing era, Lin Qing, Li Wencheng, and others had raised rebellion through the Eight Trigrams teaching; though they had been executed, at the grave pagoda at Luanzhou tun in Jixian County their deity was still worshipped under the name "Eternal Mother without Birth," and adherents of the teaching remained numerous.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiaqing reign, Lin Qing and Li Wencheng had stirred rebellion in the name of the Eight Trigrams sect. After their execution, the grave pagoda at Luanzhou tun in Jixian still honored their god as the "Eternal Mother," and many locals continued to follow the cult.

sentences.zh: 御史黃爵滋以為言，命桂良察治，毀其墳廟，廉得河南境內無生廟三十九所，並毀之；

translations.literal: Censor Huang Juesi reported on this; Gui Liang was ordered to investigate and rectify the matter, demolish the grave temples, and through investigation found thirty-nine "Eternal Mother" shrines within Henan, all of which were likewise destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: When censor Huang Juesi brought the matter to court, Gui Liang was ordered to investigate. He tore down the cult shrines and, on inquiry, found thirty-nine "Eternal Mother" temples across Henan and had them all demolished as well;

sentences.zh: 地方官失察，譴黜有差。

translations.literal: local officials who had failed in oversight were reprimanded and demoted to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: local officials who had failed to detect the cult were censured and demoted according to their degree of fault.

sentences.zh: 十九年，擢湖廣總督，調閩浙，又調雲貴。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang, transferred to Fujian and Zhejiang, and again transferred to Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 19 he became governor-general of Huguang, then was moved to Fujian-Zhejiang and afterward to Yunnan-Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 二十年，兼署雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he additionally served as acting governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 20 he also served as acting governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 滇省多盜，奏定緝捕章程；

translations.literal: Yunnan had many bandits; he memorialized to fix regulations for pursuit and capture;
translations.idiomatic: Because banditry was rife in Yunnan, he submitted regulations for pursuit and arrest;

sentences.zh: 又請迤南、迤西、迤東各標營官兵責成巡道就近稽察。

translations.literal: and further requested that the troops of the southern, western, and eastern garrison banners be charged to the circuit intendants for inspection nearby.
translations.idiomatic: and asked that troops of the southern, western, and eastern banner camps be placed under nearby circuit intendants for local inspection.

sentences.zh: 時貴州諸苗蠢動，鎮遠、黎平、都勻、古州苗尤悍，州縣不能制，疏請遴勁兵專主剿捕。

translations.literal: At the time the Miao of Guizhou were stirring everywhere; those of Zhenyuan, Liping, Duyun, and Guzhou were especially fierce, and prefectures and counties could not control them, so he memorialized to select crack troops devoted solely to suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Miao uprisings spread across Guizhou; those in Zhenyuan, Liping, Duyun, and Guzhou were especially fierce and beyond county control, so he asked that elite troops be chosen for a dedicated suppression campaign.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，入覲，留京，署兵部尚書，兼正白旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he came to court audience, remained in the capital, served as acting minister of War, and concurrently held the post of commander of the Han Army of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 25 he came to audience, stayed in the capital as acting minister of War, and concurrently commanded the Han Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 尋出為熱河都統。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he went out as commander of Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed commander of the Rehe garrison.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，召來京，以其女妻皇六子奕訢，授鑲紅旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he was summoned to the capital; his daughter was given in marriage to the emperor's sixth son Yixin, and he was appointed commander of the Han Army of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 28 he was recalled to Beijing, his daughter was married to the sixth imperial son Yixin, and he was made commander of the Han Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，署吏部尚書，出為福州將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng, he served as acting minister of Personnel and went out as general of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 1 (1851) he acted as minister of Personnel, then was posted as general of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，召授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was summoned and appointed minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2 he was recalled and appointed minister of War.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵匪陷江寧，京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Cantonese rebels took Jiangning, and the capital was placed under martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 the Taiping rebels seized Nanjing, and Beijing was put on martial alert.

sentences.zh: 桂良疏請各城門稽查增派八旗章京兵丁，補葺城上兵房，從之。

translations.literal: Gui Liang memorialized requesting increased inspection at each city gate with additional Eight Banner clerks and soldiers, and repairs to the soldiers' quarters atop the walls; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Liang asked that gate inspections be strengthened with more Banner officers and troops and that the watchrooms on the walls be repaired; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，粵匪竄河北，直隸總督訥爾經額出省防剿，命桂良駐保定為後路聲援，兼防西路要隘。

translations.literal: Before long the Cantonese rebels raided into Hebei; Governor-General Na'erjing'e went out of the province to defend and suppress them, and Gui Liang was ordered to station at Baoding as rear support and also to guard key passes on the western route.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels pushed into Hebei. While Governor-General Na'erjing'e marched out to fight them, Gui Liang was ordered to hold Baoding as a rear base and guard the western passes.

sentences.zh: 望都、唐縣土匪起，捕誅之。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Wangdu and Tang counties; he captured and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Wangdu and Tang counties, he captured and executed the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，賊由山西犯畿南，訥爾經額師潰於臨洺關，隆平、柏鄉相繼陷。

translations.literal: That autumn the rebels invaded the southern capital region from Shanxi; Na'erjing'e's army was routed at Linming Pass, and Longping and Baixiang fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the rebels entered the capital region from Shanxi. Na'erjing'e's army was routed at Linming Pass, and Longping and Baixiang fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 訥爾經額褫職逮治，授桂良直隸總督，詔責偕都統勝保速籌防剿。

translations.literal: Na'erjing'e was stripped of office and arrested for trial; Gui Liang was appointed governor-general of Zhili, and an edict rebuked him to join Grand Secretary Sengbao in swiftly planning defense and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Na'erjing'e was dismissed and arrested; Gui Liang was made governor-general of Zhili and ordered, together with Grand Secretary Sengbao, to organize defense and pursuit without delay.

sentences.zh: 布政使張集馨出兵遷延，劾罷之。

translations.literal: Provincial treasurer Zhang Jixin delayed in taking the field; Gui Liang impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: When provincial treasurer Zhang Jixin was slow to march, Gui Liang impeached him and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 賊竄正定、定州、深州、河間、天津，勢剽甚，於是桂良率提督張殿元守保定，科爾沁郡王僧格林沁統大兵駐通州衛京師，勝保督師進剿。

translations.literal: The rebels raided through Zhengding, Dingzhou, Shenzhou, Hejian, and Tianjin with fierce momentum; thereupon Gui Liang led Regional Commander Zhang Dianyuan to hold Baoding, Prince Senggelinqin of Horqin commanded the main force stationed at Tongzhou to guard the capital, and Sengbao directed the army in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels swept through Zhengding, Dingzhou, Shenzhou, Hejian, and Tianjin with great ferocity. Gui Liang held Baoding with Regional Commander Zhang Dianyuan; Prince Senggelinqin of Horqin camped at Tongzhou with the main army to shield the capital; and Sengbao led the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 四年，大捷於獨流鎮，賊走踞阜城，又走連鎮，僧格林沁、勝保會攻，賊分竄山東，勝保追擊之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, a great victory was won at Duliuzhen; the rebels fled and held Fucheng, then fled again to Lianzhen; Senggelinqin and Sengbao attacked together, the rebels split and fled into Shandong, and Sengbao pursued them.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 4 the Qing won a major victory at Duliuzhen. The rebels withdrew to Fucheng, then to Lianzhen. Senggelinqin and Sengbao attacked jointly; when the rebels split and fled into Shandong, Sengbao pursued.

sentences.zh: 桂良遣張殿元赴武邑防堵，劾散秩大臣穆輅、健銳營翼長雙僖縱兵傷官擾民，議譴。

translations.literal: Gui Liang sent Zhang Dianyuan to Wuyi for blocking defense, and impeached the honorary grand secretary Mulu and Jianruiying wing commander Shuangxi for letting their troops wound officials and harass the people; their punishment was deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Liang sent Zhang Dianyuan to block the rebels at Wuyi and impeached honorary grand secretary Mulu and Jianruiying wing commander Shuangxi for allowing their men to assault officials and terrorize civilians; the court deliberated their punishment.

sentences.zh: 秋，英吉利、美利堅兩國兵船至大沽。

translations.literal: In autumn, warships of England and the United States arrived at Dagu.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn British and American warships appeared at Dagu.

sentences.zh: 時賊氛未靖，詔戒張皇，命桂良相機辦理。

translations.literal: At the time the rebel threat was not yet settled; an edict warned against alarm and ordered Gui Liang to handle matters as circumstances allowed.
translations.idiomatic: With the rebellion still unsettled, the throne warned against panic and told Gui Liang to handle the foreigners as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 尋以前任鹽政崇綸歸調遣，令赴天津會議。

translations.literal: Soon the former salt controller Chonglun was recalled to his command and ordered to go to Tianjin for negotiations.
translations.idiomatic: Former salt controller Chonglun was soon recalled and sent to Tianjin to join the talks.

sentences.zh: 英酋咆呤要索十六條，欲遣官駐京及踐廣州入城之約，中外官平禮接見，通商稅則變通舊約；

translations.literal: The English chief Bowring demanded sixteen articles, wishing to send officials to reside in the capital and fulfill the agreement on entry into Guangzhou, equal ceremonial reception between Chinese and foreign officials, and revision of commercial tariffs under the old treaties;
translations.idiomatic: The British plenipotentiary Bowring pressed sixteen demands: resident ministers in Beijing, fulfillment of the Guangzhou entry agreement, equal ceremonial status for Chinese and foreign officials, and revised commercial tariffs;

sentences.zh: 美酋麥蓮則僅言通商一端。

translations.literal: the American chief Reed spoke only of the matter of trade.
translations.idiomatic: the American envoy Reed raised only trade issues.

sentences.zh: 崇綸等嚴拒其駐京，餘事令赴廣東聽總督查辦。

translations.literal: Chonglun and others sternly refused residence in the capital; on the remaining matters they were told to go to Guangdong and await handling by the governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: Chonglun and his colleagues firmly refused a legation in the capital and referred the rest to the governor-general of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 屢議無要領，咆呤等尋去。

translations.literal: Repeated negotiations yielded no essentials, and Bowring and the others soon departed.
translations.idiomatic: Talks dragged on without result, and Bowring's fleet eventually withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五年，僧格林沁連大破賊，賊首林鳳祥、李開芳先後就擒伏誅，畿輔肅清。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Senggelinqin repeatedly inflicted great defeats on the rebels; the rebel leaders Lin Fengxiang and Li Kaifang were captured in succession and executed, and the capital region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 5 Senggelinqin won a series of crushing victories. Rebel commanders Lin Fengxiang and Li Kaifang were captured and executed in turn, and the capital region was cleared.

sentences.zh: 七年，召拜東閣大學士，管理刑部，兼正藍旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was summoned and appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, directed the Ministry of Punishments, and concurrently served as commander of the Mongol Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 7 he was recalled as Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, placed in charge of the Ministry of Punishments, and made commander of the Mongol Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 八年春，英、法、俄、美四國聯軍北犯，毀大沽砲台，泊天津城下，聲言將犯京師。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, allied armies of England, France, Russia, and the United States invaded northward, destroyed the Dagu batteries, anchored below Tianjin, and declared they would attack the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xianfeng 8 the British, French, Russian, and American allied fleets advanced north, destroyed the Dagu forts, anchored off Tianjin, and threatened Beijing.

sentences.zh: 倉猝援軍未集，命桂良偕尚書花沙納往議。

translations.literal: Relief troops had not gathered in the emergency; Gui Liang was ordered to go with Minister Huashana to negotiate.
translations.idiomatic: Before reinforcements could assemble, Gui Liang was sent with Minister Huashana to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 敵情猖肆，要求益多：以遣官駐京、內江通商、內地遊行、兵費賠償後，始交還廣東省城。

translations.literal: The enemy's demands grew ever more insolent: only after resident ministers in the capital, inland river trade, inland travel, and indemnity for military expenses would they return Guangzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: The allies grew bolder and added demands: resident ministers in Beijing, inland navigation and trade, inland travel rights, and war indemnities must be granted before Guangzhou would be returned.

sentences.zh: 四事廷議不允。

translations.literal: The court deliberated and would not agree to the four matters.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused all four.

sentences.zh: 復起故大學士耆英同與議，英人尤不悅，拒之，耆英以擅回京獲罪。

translations.literal: The former grand secretary Qiying was again brought in to negotiate together; the English were especially displeased, rejected him, and Qiying was punished for returning to the capital without authorization.
translations.idiomatic: Former grand secretary Qiying was recalled to assist, but the British rejected him outright. Qiying was punished for returning to Beijing without leave.

sentences.zh: 桂良等議久不決，廷臣多主戰，實不足恃，而敵日以進兵為恐哧。

translations.literal: Gui Liang and the others deliberated long without resolution; many court officials favored war, but in fact that was not to be relied upon, while the enemy daily used the threat of advancing troops as intimidation.
translations.idiomatic: Negotiations under Gui Liang dragged on. Many officials urged war, but the army was in no condition to fight, and the allies daily threatened to march on the capital.

sentences.zh: 俄、美兩國調停其間，卒徇所請定議，而通商稅則俟於上海詳定之。

translations.literal: Russia and the United States mediated between them; in the end the requests were granted and an agreement settled, while commercial tariffs were to be worked out in detail later at Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: Russia and the United States mediated, and the court finally conceded. Commercial tariffs were left for detailed negotiation at Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 五月，簽約退兵，遂命桂良偕花沙納赴上海，武備院卿明善、刑部員外郎段承實副之，會同兩江總督何桂清議稅則。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, after signing the treaty the armies withdrew; Gui Liang was then ordered to go with Huashana to Shanghai, with Director of the Armory Mingshan and Vice Director of Punishments Duan Chengshi as deputies, to join Governor-General He Guiqing of the Two Jiangs in deliberating tariffs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, after the treaty was signed and the armies withdrew, Gui Liang and Huashana were sent to Shanghai with Mingshan and Duan Chengshi as deputies to work with Governor-General He Guiqing on the tariff schedule.

sentences.zh: 文宗憤和約之成出於不得已，或獻策許全免入口稅以市惠，冀改易駐京諸條，密授桂良等機宜。

translations.literal: The Wenzong Emperor, angry that the treaty had been concluded from necessity, was advised by some to grant complete exemption of import duties to win favor, hoping to alter the articles on residence in the capital, and secretly gave Gui Liang and the others his instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong resented that the treaty had been forced on him. Some advisers suggested waiving all import duties as a concession to win revision of the legation clause, and the emperor secretly instructed Gui Liang accordingly.

sentences.zh: 八月，至上海，晉文華殿大學士，授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, he reached Shanghai, was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall, and appointed an imperial body minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he reached Shanghai, was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall, and made an imperial body minister.

sentences.zh: 桂清力言免稅之不可，改約之難成，桂良亦贊其議，上甚怒，必責其補救一二端，而各國因廣東民團仍與為難，且出示偽載諭旨，堅欲罷兩廣總督黃宗漢，停撤民團。

translations.literal: He Guiqing strongly argued that duty exemption was impossible and treaty revision hard to achieve; Gui Liang also endorsed his view. The emperor was greatly angry and insisted they make up for it in one or two points. Meanwhile the foreign powers, because Guangdong militia still clashed with them, even produced a falsely printed imperial edict and firmly demanded the dismissal of Governor-General Huang Zonghan of the Two Guangs and a halt to disbanding the militia.
translations.idiomatic: He Guiqing argued forcefully that duty waivers were impossible and treaty revision unrealistic; Gui Liang agreed. The emperor was furious and demanded some concession in return. Meanwhile the powers, citing clashes with Guangdong militia and even a forged imperial edict, insisted on removing Governor-General Huang Zonghan and keeping the militia intact.

sentences.zh: 桂良等疏聞，乃解宗漢通商大臣，改授桂清。

translations.literal: Gui Liang and the others memorialized the throne; Huang Zonghan was then removed as commissioner of trade and the post was given to He Guiqing.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui Liang reported this to court, Huang Zonghan was removed as trade commissioner and He Guiqing was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 桂良等噤不敢言罷駐京諸事，先議稅則。

translations.literal: Gui Liang and the others dared not speak of abolishing the matters of residence in the capital and turned first to deliberating tariffs.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Liang and his colleagues dared not reopen the legation question and turned to the tariff talks.

sentences.zh: 十二月，英使額羅金遽率兵船赴廣東，遂罷議。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the English envoy Elgin suddenly led warships to Guangdong, and the negotiations were suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the British envoy Elgin suddenly sailed for Guangdong with his fleet, and the talks were broken off.

sentences.zh: 九年，回京，僅美利堅一國遵換通商之約，英軍复犯大沽，僧格林沁預設備，兵至，擊退之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he returned to the capital; only the United States observed the treaty on renewal of trade, while the English army again attacked Dagu; Senggelinqin had made preparations in advance, and when the troops arrived, they were beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 9 he returned to Beijing. Only the United States honored the revised trade treaty. When the British attacked Dagu again, Senggelinqin's prepared defenses drove them off.

sentences.zh: 十年，英法聯軍大舉來犯，我師失利。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Anglo-French allied armies came in force; our forces were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 10 the Anglo-French allies invaded in force and the Qing army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 七月，復命桂良赴天津議和，要增兵費，入京換約，嚴詔拒絕。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Gui Liang was again ordered to Tianjin to negotiate peace; they demanded increased military expenses and treaty exchange in the capital; stern edicts refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Gui Liang was again sent to Tianjin. The allies demanded a larger indemnity and treaty ratification in Beijing, but stern edicts ordered refusal.

sentences.zh: 敵陷天津，進逼京師，上幸熱河，恭親王奕訢留守主撫議，桂良與焉。

translations.literal: The enemy took Tianjin and pressed on the capital; the emperor went to Rehe; Prince Gong Yixin remained to direct appeasement and negotiation, and Gui Liang took part.
translations.idiomatic: The allies seized Tianjin and advanced on Beijing. The emperor fled to Rehe while Prince Gong Yixin stayed behind to negotiate; Gui Liang assisted him.

sentences.zh: 九月，於禮部換約，視八年原議益增條款，事具邦交志。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the treaty was exchanged at the Ministry of Rites; compared with the original agreement of the eighth year, the articles were further increased; the matter is fully recorded in the treatises on foreign relations.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the treaty was exchanged at the Ministry of Rites with even harsher terms than those of Xianfeng 8; the details appear in the treatises on foreign relations.

sentences.zh: 尋命督辦各國通商事務。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to supervise trade affairs with the various nations.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed to supervise trade with the foreign powers.

sentences.zh: 十一年，穆宗即位，回京，命在軍機大臣上行走。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the Muzong Emperor acceded, he returned to the capital and was ordered to serve on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 11, after the Tongzhi Emperor's accession, he returned to Beijing and was appointed to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，卒，優恤，贈太傅，祀賢良祠，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he died; exceptional condolence gifts were granted, he was posthumously given the title of Grand Tutor, enshrined in the Temple of Worthies, and given the posthumous name Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tongzhi 1 (1862). The court granted exceptional mourning honors, posthumously titled him Grand Tutor, enshrined him in the Temple of Worthies, and gave him the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 瑞麟，字澄泉，葉赫那喇氏，滿洲正藍旗人。

translations.literal: Rui Lin, courtesy name Chengquan, of the Yehe Nara clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Lin, styled Chengquan, was a Yehe Nara Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 由文生充太常寺讀祝官，補贊禮郎。

translations.literal: From a civil licentiate he served as reader of sacrificial prayers in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was appointed a ceremonial usher.
translations.idiomatic: A civil licentiate, he served as reader of sacrificial prayers in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was appointed ceremonial usher.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年，祫祭太廟，讀祝洪亮，宣宗嘉之，賜五品頂戴、花翎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, at the joint autumn sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, his reading of the prayer was resonant; the Xuanzong Emperor praised him and granted a fifth-rank official cap button and peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: At the Daoguang 27 joint autumn sacrifice in the Ancestral Temple, his prayer reading was so resonant that the Xuanzong Emperor praised him and awarded a fifth-rank cap button and peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，超擢太常寺少卿，又擢內閣學士，兼管太常寺。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he was promoted out of turn to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then again promoted to a Hanlin academician of the Grand Secretariat and given concurrent charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 28 he was rapidly promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then to Grand Secretariat academician with concurrent charge of that court.

sentences.zh: 三十年，擢禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, he was promoted to vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 30 he became vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，兼鑲藍旗滿洲副都統、正黃旗護軍統領。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng, he concurrently served as vice commander of the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and commander of the guard corps of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 1 he also served as vice commander of the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and commander of the Plain Yellow Banner guard corps.

sentences.zh: 三年，調戶部，命在軍機大臣上行走。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and ordered to serve on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 he was moved to the Ministry of Revenue and appointed to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪竄畿輔，踞靜海縣及獨流鎮，命瑞麟率兵從僧格林沁防剿，會攻獨流，克之。

translations.literal: At the time the Cantonese rebels had raided into the capital region and held Jinghai County and Duliuzhen; Rui Lin was ordered to lead troops with Senggelinqin in defense and suppression, and in a joint attack on Duliuzhen they took it.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels raided the capital region and held Jinghai and Duliuzhen, Rui Lin was ordered to campaign with Senggelinqin; their joint assault captured Duliuzhen.

sentences.zh: 靜海賊竄陷阜城，又分竄連鎮及山東高唐州，瑞麟合擊，屢有擒斬。

translations.literal: The rebels at Jinghai fled and took Fucheng, then split and fled to Lianzhen and Gaotang prefecture in Shandong; Rui Lin attacked jointly and repeatedly captured and killed the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinghai rebels fled to Fucheng, then split toward Lianzhen and Gaotang in Shandong. Rui Lin joined the pursuit and won repeated captures and kills.

sentences.zh: 五年，克連鎮，賊首林鳳祥就擒，加都統銜，賜號巴達瑯阿巴圖魯，授西安將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Lianzhen was taken and the rebel leader Lin Fengxiang was captured; Rui Lin was given the rank of commander-in-chief, granted the title Badarang Abaturu, and appointed general of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 5 Lianzhen fell and Lin Fengxiang was captured. Rui Lin received commander-in-chief rank, the title Badarang Abaturu, and appointment as general of Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢禮部尚書，兼鑲白旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to minister of Rites and concurrently made commander of the Mongol Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he became minister of Rites and commander of the Mongol Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 八年，英兵犯天津，命馳赴楊村籌防。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when English troops attacked Tianjin, he was ordered to hurry to Yangcun to organize defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 8, when the British attacked Tianjin, he was rushed to Yangcun to organize defenses.

sentences.zh: 洎撫議定，敵退。

translations.literal: When appeasement and negotiation were settled, the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was negotiated, the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 文宗知和不可恃，亟治海防，命瑞麟赴天津修築大沽砲台。

translations.literal: The Wenzong Emperor knew peace could not be relied upon and urgently strengthened coastal defense, ordering Rui Lin to go to Tianjin to repair and build the Dagu batteries.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing peace could not be trusted, Emperor Wenzong urgently strengthened coastal defenses and sent Rui Lin to rebuild the Dagu forts.

sentences.zh: 尋署直隸總督，增建雙港砲台，調福建霆船戰船，增募水師。

translations.literal: Soon he served as acting governor-general of Zhili, additionally built batteries at Shuanggang, transferred battle junks from Fujian, and increased recruitment of naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: He soon acted as governor-general of Zhili, added batteries at Shuanggang, transferred Fujian war junks, and expanded the naval force.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁移師天津，分駐要隘。

translations.literal: Senggelinqin moved his army to Tianjin and stationed detachments at key passes.
translations.idiomatic: Senggelinqin moved his army to Tianjin and posted detachments at key points.

sentences.zh: 瑞麟回京，調戶部尚書緦拜文淵閣大學士，兼管禮部鴻臚寺、太常寺。

translations.literal: Rui Lin returned to the capital, was transferred to minister of Revenue, and was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, with concurrent charge of the Court of State Ceremonial and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices under the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Lin returned to Beijing, became minister of Revenue, and was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion with concurrent charge of the Court of State Ceremonial and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 九年，管理戶部。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he directed the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 9 he took charge of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十年，充殿試讀卷官，授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he served as reader of palace examination papers and was appointed an imperial body minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 10 he served as reader of palace examination papers and was made an imperial body minister.

sentences.zh: 六月，英法聯軍复犯天津，命率京兵萬人守通州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Anglo-French allied armies again attacked Tianjin; he was ordered to lead ten thousand capital troops to guard Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Anglo-French allies attacked Tianjin again, and he was ordered to hold Tongzhou with ten thousand capital troops.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁屢戰失利，敵軍進通州，瑞麟偕勝保御之八里橋，左右夾擊，勝保傷砲墜馬，軍潰，敵遂逼京師。

translations.literal: Senggelinqin suffered repeated defeats; the enemy advanced on Tongzhou; Rui Lin together with Sengbao defended at Baliqiao with attacks from both flanks; Sengbao was wounded by cannon fire and fell from his horse, the army was routed, and the enemy then pressed on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Senggelinqin's repeated defeats the enemy advanced on Tongzhou. Rui Lin and Sengbao met them at Baliqiao in a pincer attack, but Sengbao was wounded by cannon fire and thrown from his horse, the army collapsed, and the enemy pressed toward Beijing.

sentences.zh: 瑞麟迎戰安定門外，敗績，褫職。

translations.literal: Rui Lin met the enemy outside the Anding Gate, was defeated, and was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Lin fought again outside the Anding Gate, was defeated, and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸熱河，命扈從行在。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went to Rehe, he was ordered to attend the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled to Rehe, he was ordered to accompany the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，和議成，予侍郎銜，隨僧格林沁剿山東捻匪。

translations.literal: That winter, when peace was concluded, he was given the rank of vice minister and followed Senggelinqin in suppressing the Nian bandits of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, after peace was made, he was restored to vice-minister rank and joined Senggelinqin against the Shandong Nian rebels.

sentences.zh: 攻鉅野羊山集賊巢，失利，馬蹶被傷，退軍濟寧，复褫職，召回京。

translations.literal: Attacking the rebel nest at Yangshanji in Juye, he was defeated; his horse stumbled and he was wounded, withdrew to Jining, was again stripped of office, and recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An assault on the rebel stronghold at Yangshanji in Juye failed; his horse stumbled and he was wounded. He withdrew to Jining, was dismissed again, and recalled to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授鑲黃旗漢軍都統，管神機營事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was appointed commander of the Han Army of the Bordered Yellow Banner and directed affairs of the Shenjiying firearms corps.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 11 he was made commander of the Han Bordered Yellow Banner and placed in charge of the Shenjiying firearms corps.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，出為熱河都統，疏請招佃圍邊荒地八千頃充練餉，允之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he went out as commander of Rehe and memorialized requesting tenant recruitment for eight thousand qing of wasteland on the border of the imperial hunting grounds to supply drill funds; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1 he was posted as commander of Rehe and asked to open eight thousand qing of border wasteland for tenants to fund militia training; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 二年，調廣州將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to general of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 2 he was transferred to general of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，兼署兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he additionally served as acting governor-general of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 4 he also served as acting governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 信宜、化州土匪起，遣兵平之。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Xinyi and Huazhou; he sent troops and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Xinyi and Huazhou, he sent troops and suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 粵匪汪海洋由福建竄廣東大埔，遣副將方耀擊走之。

translations.literal: The Cantonese rebel Wang Haiyang raided from Fujian into Dabu in Guangdong; Deputy Commander Fang Yao was sent and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Wang Haiyang raided from Fujian into Dabu, Guangdong, Rui Lin sent Deputy Commander Fang Yao to drive him back.

sentences.zh: 入閩會剿，复詔安、平和。

translations.literal: Entering Fujian for joint suppression, he recovered Zhao'an and Pinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed into Fujian for joint operations and recovered Zhao'an and Pinghe.

sentences.zh: 賊复竄廣東境，連敗之於長樂、鎮平。

translations.literal: The rebels again raided into Guangdong territory; he defeated them repeatedly at Changle and Zhenping.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels re-entered Guangdong, he defeated them repeatedly at Changle and Zhenping.

sentences.zh: 時賊踪往來於福建、廣東、江西界上，瑞麟偕左宗棠疏請三省會剿。

translations.literal: At the time rebel tracks moved back and forth on the borders of Fujian, Guangdong, and Jiangxi; Rui Lin together with Zuo Zongtang memorialized requesting joint suppression by the three provinces.
translations.idiomatic: As rebel bands shuttled across the Fujian-Guangdong-Jiangxi borderlands, Rui Lin and Zuo Zongtang asked for a three-province joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 詔提督鮑超由江西來援，四面環攻。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Regional Commander Bao Chao to come from Jiangxi in support, and attacks encircled them on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Bao Chao was ordered from Jiangxi to reinforce, and the allies closed in from four sides.

sentences.zh: 十二月，殲偽偕王譚體元於黃沙壩，擒首逆汪海洋，誅之，餘賊肅清。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the false co-prince Tan Tiyuan was destroyed at Huangshaba, the chief rebel Wang Haiyang was captured and executed, and the remaining rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the false co-prince Tan Tiyuan was killed at Huangshaba, rebel leader Wang Haiyang was captured and executed, and the remaining rebels were cleared.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，優詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: When news of the victory arrived, an edict of special praise and reward was issued.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued an edict of special commendation when victory was reported.

sentences.zh: 五年，實授兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was formally appointed governor-general of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 5 he received formal appointment as governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 廣東素多盜，伏莽時起。

translations.literal: Guangdong had always had many bandits, and hidden ruffians rose from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had long been troubled by bandits, and outlaw gangs surfaced constantly.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫蔣益澧號知兵，瑞麟部將方耀、鄭紹忠皆能戰，先後破斬五坑客匪，曹沖、赤溪及新安、東莞諸匪，潮州、瓊州洋盜、土匪。

translations.literal: At the time Governor Jiang Yisui was known as skilled in military affairs; Rui Lin's subordinate commanders Fang Yao and Zheng Shaozhong were both able fighters; they successively defeated and killed the Hakka bandits of Wukeng, the bandits of Caochong, Chixi, and Xin'an and Dongguan, and the foreign pirates and local bandits of Chaozhou and Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Jiang Yisui was reputed as a capable commander, and Rui Lin's generals Fang Yao and Zheng Shaozhong were skilled fighters. Together they crushed the Wukeng Hakka bandits, outlaws in Caochong, Chixi, Xin'an, and Dongguan, and pirates and bandits in Chaozhou and Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，兼署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he additionally served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 9 he also served as acting governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 十年，復拜文淵閣大學士，仍留總督任。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was again appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and still retained the post of governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 10 he was again made Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion while remaining governor-general.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒，詔嘉前勞，贈太保，祀賢良祠，諡文莊。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he died; an edict praised his former labors, granted him the posthumous title of Grand Guardian, enshrined him in the Temple of Worthies, and gave the posthumous name Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tongzhi 13. The court praised his earlier service, posthumously titled him Grand Guardian, enshrined him in the Temple of Worthies, and gave him the posthumous name Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 子懷塔布，由廕生授刑部主事，晉員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Huai Tabu, through yinsheng privilege, was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments and promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huai Tabu entered office by inheritance as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments and rose to vice director.

sentences.zh: 以父卹典擢四品京堂，累遷禮部尚書，充內務府大臣。

translations.literal: Through the mourning honors for his father he was promoted to a fourth-rank capital official, was repeatedly transferred to minister of Rites, and served as a minister of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning honors for his father raised him to a fourth-rank capital post; he later became minister of Rites and served on the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十四年，主事王照上書言事，久之始代奏，坐違旨抑格，褫職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu, Principal Secretary Wang Zhao submitted a memorial on state affairs; only after a long delay did Huai Tabu present it on his behalf; he was punished for violating the imperial order and suppressing the memorial, and was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 24 principal secretary Wang Zhao submitted a reform memorial that Huai Tabu long withheld before forwarding. He was dismissed for defying the throne and suppressing the petition.

sentences.zh: 未幾，皇太后訓政，起授左都御史，复充​​內務府大臣，遷理籓院尚書。

translations.literal: Before long, when the empress dowager assumed regency, he was restored and appointed left censor-in-chief, again served as minister of the Imperial Household Department, and was transferred to minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after the empress dowager resumed regency, he was restored as left censor-in-chief, again joined the Imperial Household Department, and became minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，卒，贈太子少保，諡恪勤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, he died; he was posthumously given the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Keqin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Guangxu 26 and was posthumously titled Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the name Keqin.

sentences.zh: 官文，字秀峰，王佳氏，滿洲正白旗人，先隸內務府正白旗漢軍。

translations.literal: Guan Wen, courtesy name Xiufeng, of the Wanggiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner and had earlier been attached to the Han Army of the Plain White Banner under the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen, styled Xiufeng, was a Wanggiya Manchu of the Plain White Banner who had earlier belonged to the Han Plain White Banner under the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 由拜唐阿補藍翎侍衛，累擢頭等侍衛。

translations.literal: From a baitangga he was appointed a bodyguard with the blue tail feather, and was repeatedly promoted to first-class bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from a junior guard to a blue-tail bodyguard and eventually to first-class bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年，出為廣州漢軍副都統，調荊州右翼副都統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang, he went out as Han Army vice commander of Guangzhou and was transferred to vice commander of the Right Wing at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 21 he became Han Army vice commander at Guangzhou, then was transferred to the Right Wing vice command at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 粵匪既陷漢陽，將犯荊州。

translations.literal: After the Cantonese rebels had taken Hanyang, they were about to attack Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels seized Hanyang, they threatened Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，將軍台湧駐防德安，命官文專統荊州防兵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, General Tai Yong garrisoned De'an, and Guan Wen was ordered to command exclusively the defensive troops of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 General Tai Yong garrisoned De'an while Guan Wen was given sole command of Jingzhou's defense force.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢荊州將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was promoted to general of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 4 he was promoted to general of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊陷安陸、荊門、宜昌。

translations.literal: The rebels took Anlu, Jingmen, and Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels captured Anlu, Jingmen, and Yichang.

sentences.zh: 時荊州兵多調赴武昌，分屯要隘，城中兵僅二千。

translations.literal: At the time most Jingzhou troops had been transferred to Wuchang and posted at key passes; troops in the city numbered only two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Most Jingzhou troops had been sent to Wuchang and posted at key passes, leaving only two thousand men in the city.

sentences.zh: 監利又陷，官文遣軍復之；

translations.literal: Jianli fell again; Guan Wen sent troops and recovered it;
translations.idiomatic: When Jianli fell again, Guan Wen sent troops and recovered it;

sentences.zh: 連复宜昌、石首、華容，於是荊州稍安，而武昌被圍急，官文遣將沿漢下援。

translations.literal: he recovered Yichang, Shishou, and Huarong in succession; Jingzhou was thus somewhat settled, but Wuchang was urgently besieged, and Guan Wen sent generals down the Han to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: then recovered Yichang, Shishou, and Huarong in turn, easing pressure on Jingzhou. Wuchang remained under siege, so he sent generals down the Han to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 六月，武昌复失守，命官文統籌全局，規复武漢。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Wuchang was again lost; Guan Wen was ordered to coordinate the overall situation and plan recovery of Wuhan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Wuchang fell again. Guan Wen was ordered to take overall command and plan the recovery of Wuhan.

sentences.zh: 因疏言：「賊情詭譎，軍情隨時變幻。

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized, saying: "The rebels are cunning and devious, and military conditions change from moment to moment.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The rebels are cunning, and the military situation shifts constantly.

sentences.zh: 武漢之賊一日不盡，荊州不得安枕。

translations.literal: Until the rebels at Wuhan are not eliminated for a single day, Jingzhou cannot rest secure.
translations.idiomatic: Until Wuhan is cleared, Jingzhou cannot be secure.

sentences.zh: 賊踞漢陽，倚江為險，絕我糧道，阻我援軍。

translations.literal: The rebels hold Hanyang, relying on the river as a barrier, cutting off our grain routes and blocking our relief armies.
translations.idiomatic: They hold Hanyang, using the river as a barrier to cut our supply lines and block reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 今欲复武昌，必先攻漢陽，奪賊所恃之險，而後武昌可圖也。

translations.literal: If we now wish to recover Wuchang, we must first attack Hanyang, seize the strong points the rebels rely on, and only then can Wuchang be taken.
translations.idiomatic: To retake Wuchang we must first attack Hanyang and seize the positions they rely on; only then can Wuchang be taken.

sentences.zh: 總兵雙保自潛江進剿，兵力過單。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Shuangbao advances from Qianjiang to suppress them, but his force is too weak.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Shuangbao is advancing from Qianjiang, but his force is too thin.

sentences.zh: 臣已令羅遵殿以戰船百艘自仙桃鎮、蔡店迳趨漢陽，與撫臣楊霈分道夾攻；

translations.literal: Your servant has already ordered Luo Zundian with a hundred war junks to strike directly at Hanyang from Xiantao town and Caidian, and to attack jointly from separate routes with Governor Yang Pi;
translations.idiomatic: I have ordered Luo Zundian with a hundred war junks to strike Hanyang from Xiantao and Caidian while Governor Yang Pi attacks from another direction;

sentences.zh: 又檄總兵福炘往助雙保，知縣吳振鏞進复沔陽以通餉道。

translations.literal: I have also ordered Regional Commander Fuxin to assist Shuangbao, and Magistrate Wu Zhenyong to advance and recover Mianyang to open the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: I have also ordered Regional Commander Fuxin to reinforce Shuangbao and Magistrate Wu Zhenyong to recover Mianyang and reopen the supply line.

sentences.zh: 惟賊踞岳州，南北援軍均受牽制，尤應先剿岳州之賊。

translations.literal: Only the rebels hold Yuezhou, tying down relief armies north and south; we should especially first suppress the rebels at Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because the rebels hold Yuezhou and tie down forces north and south, Yuezhou must be cleared first.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓方統砲船駐湘陰，塔齊布之師已入岳州境，臣已促其速進，分兵阻江路。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan is commanding gunboats stationed at Xiangyin; Taqibu's army has already entered Yuezhou territory; your servant has urged them to advance quickly and divide troops to block the river route.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan is at Xiangyin with gunboats, and Taqibu's army has entered Yuezhou. I have urged them to advance quickly and block the river route.

sentences.zh: 复派同知銜李光榮等率川勇防調弦口，張子銘防監利尺八口，都司宗維清沿江接應。

translations.literal: I have again dispatched Li Guangrong and others with the rank of subprefect to lead Sichuan braves to defend Diaoxiankou, Zhang Ziming to defend Chibakou at Jianli, and Brigade Commander Zong Weiqing to respond along the river.
translations.idiomatic: I have also posted Li Guangrong's Sichuan braves at Diaoxiankou, Zhang Ziming at Jianli's Chibakou, and Brigade Commander Zong Weiqing along the river for support.

sentences.zh: 荊州僅賸旗兵分守要隘，隨時接應，庶幾可進可退，不致有顧此失彼之虞。」

translations.literal: At Jingzhou only banner troops remain, posted at key passes to respond at any time, so that we may advance or withdraw and not fear losing one place while attending to another."
translations.idiomatic: At Jingzhou only banner troops remain at key passes for flexible support, so we can advance or withdraw without neglecting one front for another."

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received and noted.

sentences.zh: 尋曾國籓克岳州，賊艘悉出大江，官文遣涼州副都統魁玉、總兵楊昌泗赴螺山防江，殲賊甚多。

translations.literal: Soon Zeng Guofan took Yuezhou; rebel vessels all came out onto the great river; Guan Wen sent Liangzhou Vice Commander Kuiyu and Regional Commander Yang Changsi to Luoshan to defend the river and destroyed many rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zeng Guofan took Yuezhou and rebel boats poured into the main river. Guan Wen sent Vice Commander Kuiyu and Regional Commander Yang Changsi to Luoshan, where they destroyed many rebels.

sentences.zh: 八月，武昌、漢陽相繼复，論功被優敘。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Wuchang and Hanyang were recovered in succession; for merit he received exceptional commendation in the records.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wuchang and Hanyang were recovered in turn, and he received special commendation for merit.

sentences.zh: 五年，總督楊霈師潰德安，漢陽、漢口復陷，德安、隨州繼之，詔褫霈職，授官文湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Governor-General Yang Pi's army was routed at De'an; Hanyang and Hankou fell again, followed by De'an and Suizhou; an edict stripped Pi of office and appointed Guan Wen governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 5 Governor-General Yang Pi was routed at De'an. Hanyang and Hankou fell again, then De'an and Suizhou. Yang Pi was dismissed and Guan Wen was made governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 師次安陸，疏言：「賊自隨州退踞德安，兇鋒疊挫。

translations.literal: As the army halted at Anlu, he memorialized, saying: "The rebels withdrew from Suizhou and hold De'an; their fierce momentum has been repeatedly checked.
translations.idiomatic: Halting at Anlu, he memorialized: "The rebels withdrew from Suizhou to De'an, and their momentum has been checked repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 惟天門、京山道路四通，儻竄襄河，勾連仙桃鎮以下股匪，不獨荊襄在在堪虞，上游各處均可北竄。

translations.literal: Only Tianmen and Jingshan have roads running in all directions; if they slip into the Xiang River region and link with bandit bands below Xiantao town, not only Jingxiang will everywhere be at risk, but all upper reaches may raid northward.
translations.idiomatic: But Tianmen and Jingshan lie on crossroads. If they slip into the Xiang River region and link with bandits below Xiantao, not only Jingxiang but the entire upper river country could be threatened from the north.

sentences.zh: 現遣兵一由天門、皁市進剿，一往京山防守，臣駐安陸為兩路應援，諮固原提督孔廣順伺隙進取，署提臣訥欽為後應。

translations.literal: I now send one force to advance from Tianmen and Zaoshi, and another to defend Jingshan; your servant remains at Anlu to support both routes, consults Guyuan Regional Commander Kong Guangshun to seize opportunities to advance, and Acting Regional Commander Neqin serves as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: I am sending one column from Tianmen and Zaoshi and another to hold Jingshan, while I remain at Anlu to support both. Regional Commander Kong Guangshun will seize openings to advance, with Acting Regional Commander Neqin in reserve.

sentences.zh: 俟欽差大臣西凌阿入楚，即統兵從襄河兩岸水陸並進，由漢川攻漢陽。」

translations.literal: When Imperial Commissioner Xiling'a enters Chu, we shall at once command troops to advance by land and water along both banks of the Xiang River and attack Hanyang through Hanchuan."
translations.idiomatic: When Imperial Commissioner Xiling'a enters Hubei, we will advance by land and water along both banks of the Xiang and attack Hanyang through Hanchuan."

sentences.zh: 秋，西凌阿戰德安失利，乃命官文代為欽差大臣，馳援德安。

translations.literal: In autumn, Xiling'a was defeated at De'an; Guan Wen was then ordered to replace him as imperial commissioner and hurry to relieve De'an.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Xiling'a was defeated at De'an, and Guan Wen replaced him as imperial commissioner and rushed to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 賊棄城走，躡追之，直搗漢陽。

translations.literal: The rebels abandoned the city and fled; he pursued them and drove straight at Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels abandoned the city and fled; he pursued them straight to Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，督兵薄西門橋，迭敗賊於龜山、尾湖堤、五顯廟，破賊卡，毀東西土城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, he led troops close to Ximen Bridge, repeatedly defeated rebels at Guishan, Weihu Embankment, and Wuxian Temple, broke rebel stockades, and destroyed the earthen walls east and west.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he pressed to Ximen Bridge, repeatedly defeated rebels at Guishan, Weihu Embankment, and Wuxian Temple, stormed their stockades, and destroyed the eastern and western earthen walls.

sentences.zh: 六年，賊造浮橋從西門分隊來犯，擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the rebels built a pontoon bridge and attacked in separate columns from the west gate; he beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 6 the rebels built a pontoon bridge and attacked in columns from the west gate; he drove them back.

sentences.zh: 分兵河口斷其糧道，令副都統都興阿攻圍風焚積聚，賊勢漸蹙。

translations.literal: He divided troops at the river mouth to cut their grain route, ordered Vice Commander Duxing'a to attack, besiege, and burn stores by wind, and the rebel position gradually tightened.
translations.idiomatic: He posted troops at the river mouth to cut supplies, ordered Vice Commander Duxing'a to besiege and burn their stores, and the rebel position steadily weakened.

sentences.zh: 秋，破漢陽城外賊營，連戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In autumn, he broke the rebel camps outside Hanyang and won successive victories.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he stormed the rebel camps outside Hanyang and won a series of victories.

sentences.zh: 巡撫胡林翼規复武昌。

translations.literal: Governor Hu Linyi planned recovery of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Hu Linyi planned the recovery of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，約同日水陸大舉，分攻武、漢，官文督軍分路進，水師擊漢陽東門，破五顯廟賊卡，李孟群又敗龜山援賊，王國才、楊昌泗由西門攻入，遂復漢陽，俘偽將軍等五百餘人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, they agreed on a same-day major land-and-water assault, dividing attacks on Wu and Han; Guan Wen directed the army advancing by separate routes; the naval force struck Hanyang's east gate, broke the rebel stockade at Wuxian Temple; Li Mengqun again defeated relief rebels at Guishan; Wang Guocai and Yang Changsi entered through the west gate; Hanyang was thus recovered, and more than five hundred false generals and others were captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they launched a coordinated land-and-water assault on Wuhan. Guan Wen led columns inland while the fleet struck Hanyang's east gate and broke the Wuxian Temple stockade. Li Mengqun defeated Guishan reinforcements; Wang Guocai and Yang Changsi entered through the west gate. Hanyang was recovered and more than five hundred rebel officers were captured.

sentences.zh: 林翼亦復武昌，詔嘉獎，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Lin Yi also recovered Wuchang; an edict praised and rewarded them, granting peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi also recovered Wuchang. The court commended them and awarded peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 七年，偕林翼疏言：「湖北為長江上游要害，武漢尤九省通衢，自來東南有事必爭之地。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, together with Lin Yi he memorialized, saying: "Hubei is the strategic key to the upper Yangzi, and Wuhan especially is the thoroughfare of nine provinces; whenever trouble arises in the southeast, it is a place that must be contested.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 7 he and Hu Linyi memorialized: "Hubei commands the upper Yangzi, and Wuhan is the crossroads of nine provinces—a prize in every southeastern crisis.

sentences.zh: 三次失陷，力攻兩載而後克之。

translations.literal: It fell three times and was taken only after two years of hard fighting.
translations.idiomatic: It fell three times and was retaken only after two years of hard fighting.

sentences.zh: 目前相機防剿，不令賊乘間上竄，蹈從前覆轍。

translations.literal: At present we defend and suppress as circumstances allow, not letting the rebels seize an opening to raid upward and repeat former disasters.
translations.idiomatic: We must defend and pursue as circumstances allow and keep the rebels from raiding upstream and repeating past disasters.

sentences.zh: 業派李續賓由南岸，都興阿、孔廣順、王國才由北岸，楊載福率水師由江路分道進剿。

translations.literal: We have already assigned Li Xubin on the south bank, Duxing'a, Kong Guangshun, and Wang Guocai on the north bank, and Yang Zaifu leading the navy along the river route to advance in separate columns.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xubin advances on the south bank; Duxing'a, Kong Guangshun, and Wang Guocai on the north; and Yang Zaifu leads the fleet upriver in separate columns.

sentences.zh: 現北岸黃州至黃梅，南岸武昌至興國，均已肅清，崇、通一帶搜捕殆盡；

translations.literal: Now from Huangzhou to Huangmei on the north bank and from Wuchang to Xingguo on the south bank, all have been pacified, and in the Chongyang-Tongcheng region pursuit is nearly complete;
translations.idiomatic: The north bank from Huangzhou to Huangmei and the south bank from Wuchang to Xingguo are now clear, and pursuit in the Chongyang-Tongcheng region is nearly complete;

sentences.zh: 李續賓抵九江，與曾國籓會合進攻；

translations.literal: Li Xubin has reached Jiujiang and joined Zeng Guofan in a joint advance;
translations.idiomatic: Li Xubin has reached Jiujiang and joined Zeng Guofan in the attack;

sentences.zh: 楊載福毀城外賊營；

translations.literal: Yang Zaifu has destroyed rebel camps outside the walls;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaifu has destroyed the rebel camps outside the walls;

sentences.zh: 惟小池口賊壘未拔，派鮑超助攻。

translations.literal: only the rebel fort at Xiaochikou has not been taken, and Bao Chao has been dispatched to assist the attack.
translations.idiomatic: only the fort at Xiaochikou remains; Bao Chao has been sent to assist.

sentences.zh: 安徽之英山、太湖、宿松、望江接壤湖北，皆為賊藪，有窺伺上犯之心。

translations.literal: Yingshan, Taihu, Susong, and Wangjiang in Anhui border Hubei; all are rebel lairs and harbor designs to watch for chances to raid upward.
translations.idiomatic: Yingshan, Taihu, Susong, and Wangjiang in Anhui border Hubei and remain rebel haunts that threaten to strike northward.

sentences.zh: 飭王國才駐黃梅之大河鋪、界嶺岩，孔廣順駐蘄水之孔隴驛，巴揚阿率馬隊為各路應援，以固楚北門戶。

translations.literal: Wang Guocai is ordered to garrison Dahepu and Jielingyan in Huangmei; Kong Guangshun to garrison Konglong Post in Qishui; Bayang'a to lead cavalry as support on all routes, to secure the northern gateway of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guocai holds Dahepu and Jielingyan in Huangmei; Kong Guangshun holds Konglong Post in Qishui; Bayang'a's cavalry supports all routes—to secure northern Hubei's gateway.

sentences.zh: 道士洑水闊溜急，田家鎮兩山對峙，水師皆難久駐，酌留各營遊巡江面，足備鎮馭。

translations.literal: At Daoshifu the water is wide and the current swift; at Tianjiazhen two mountains face each other; the navy cannot long remain at either place; we have judged it best to leave camps patrolling the river surface, sufficient to control and restrain.
translations.idiomatic: At Daoshifu the river is wide and fast; at Tianjiazhen mountains close the channel—neither suits a long naval stay. Patrol camps on the river will suffice to control the waterway.

sentences.zh: 通籌大局，我軍已據水陸上游，實蓄破竹建瓴之勢。

translations.literal: Considering the overall situation, our army already holds the upper reaches by land and water and truly possesses the momentum of splitting bamboo and pouring from a high roof.
translations.idiomatic: Taken together, our forces hold the upstream by land and water and now have overwhelming momentum.

sentences.zh: 所慮江西七府未平，武昌尚有肘腋之患。

translations.literal: What we fear is that the seven prefectures of Jiangxi are not yet pacified and Wuchang still has trouble at its very side.
translations.idiomatic: Our concern is that seven Jiangxi prefectures remain unrestored and Wuchang still faces threats at its flank.

sentences.zh: 賊若由通城、崇陽、興國竄逼武昌，反出江西各軍之上，自當固守武昌，以為後路根本。

translations.literal: If the rebels should raid toward Wuchang through Tongcheng, Chongyang, and Xingguo and emerge above the various Jiangxi armies, we should of course hold Wuchang firm as the fundamental base of our rear route.
translations.idiomatic: If rebels strike Wuchang through Tongcheng, Chongyang, and Xingguo and get behind the Jiangxi armies, we must hold Wuchang as the base of our rear.

sentences.zh: 相機籌畫，節節進取，仍步步嚴防，庶軍情無返顧掣肘之虞，轉餉有源源不竭之利。」

translations.literal: Planning as circumstances allow, advancing section by section while still guarding strictly step by step, we may hope that military affairs will have no worry of looking back or being hampered, and that transport of supplies will have the benefit of an unceasing flow."
translations.idiomatic: We should advance step by step while guarding every rear, so the army need not look back in fear and supplies may flow without end."

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received and noted.

sentences.zh: 初，官文由荊州將軍調總督，凡上游荊、市、襄、鄖諸郡兵事餉事悉主之。

translations.literal: At first, when Guan Wen was transferred from general of Jingzhou to governor-general, he directed all military affairs and supplies in the upper prefectures of Jing, Shi, Xiang, and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Wen moved from Jingzhou general to governor-general, he controlled military affairs and supplies in the upper Jing, Shi, Xiang, and Yun prefectures.

sentences.zh: 林翼以巡撫駐金口，凡下游武、漢、黃、德諸郡兵事餉事悉主之。

translations.literal: Lin Yi as governor was stationed at Jinkou and directed all military affairs and supplies in the lower prefectures of Wu, Han, Huang, and De.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi as governor at Jinkou controlled military affairs and supplies in the lower Wu, Han, Huang, and De prefectures.

sentences.zh: 南北軍各領分地，徵兵調餉，每有違言。

translations.literal: The northern and southern armies each held separate territories; in raising troops and allocating supplies there were often disputes.
translations.idiomatic: The northern and southern commands each held separate territory, and disputes over troops and funds were frequent.

sentences.zh: 武昌既复，林翼威望日起，官文自知不及，思假以為重，林翼益推誠相結納，於是吏治、財政、軍事悉聽林翼主持，官文畫諾而已。

translations.literal: After Wuchang was recovered, Lin Yi's prestige rose daily; Guan Wen knew himself unequal and wished to borrow that weight; Lin Yi all the more joined him in sincere alliance; thereupon civil administration, finance, and military affairs were all left to Lin Yi's direction, and Guan Wen merely assented.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuchang was recovered, Hu Linyi's prestige grew daily. Guan Wen knew he could not match him and sought to share in his authority; Hu Linyi responded with genuine cooperation. Civil administration, finance, and military affairs all passed to Hu Linyi, while Guan Wen merely assented.

sentences.zh: 不數年，足食足兵，東南大局，隱然以湖北為之樞。

translations.literal: Within a few years there was sufficient food and sufficient troops, and for the great situation in the southeast, Hubei quietly became its pivot.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years Hubei had ample food and troops and quietly became the pivot of the southeastern war effort.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，复九江，論功，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, Jiujiang was recovered; for merit he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Xianfeng 8 Jiujiang was recovered, and he received the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 皖賊陷麻城、黃安，圍蘄州，先後破走之。

translations.literal: Anhui rebels took Macheng and Huang'an and besieged Qizhou; he defeated and drove them off in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Anhui rebels seized Macheng and Huang'an and besieged Qizhou; he defeated and drove them off in turn.

sentences.zh: 七月，胡林翼丁母憂，官文疏請留林翼治軍，改為署理，從之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Hu Linyi entered mourning for his mother; Guan Wen memorialized requesting that Lin Yi remain to command the army and be changed to acting status; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Hu Linyi entered mourning for his mother. Guan Wen asked that he remain to command the army in an acting capacity, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 命官文暫行兼署巡撫，尋以湖廣總督協辦大學士。

translations.literal: Guan Wen was ordered temporarily to serve additionally as acting governor, and soon was made associate grand secretary with the rank of governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen was ordered to act temporarily as governor and soon received associate grand secretary rank while remaining governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 李續賓戰歿三河，皖、鄂震動。

translations.literal: Li Xubin was killed in battle at Sanhe; Anhui and Hubei were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xubin was killed at Sanhe, shaking Anhui and Hubei.

sentences.zh: 官文分兵扼蘄州、廣濟、麻城諸隘，固守九江、彭澤，水師嚴防江面，人心始定。

translations.literal: Guan Wen divided troops to hold the passes at Qizhou, Guangji, and Macheng, firmly defended Jiujiang and Pengze, and had the navy strictly guard the river surface; popular morale then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen posted troops at Qizhou, Guangji, and Macheng, held Jiujiang and Pengze firmly, and had the navy guard the river—steadying public morale.

sentences.zh: 九年，賊竄湖南，圍寶慶，檄荊宜施道李續宜赴援，大破之，寶慶圍解。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, rebels raided into Hunan and besieged Baoqing; he ordered Jing-Yi-Shi Circuit Intendant Li Xuyi to go in relief, inflicted a great defeat, and the siege of Baoqing was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 9 rebels raided Hunan and besieged Baoqing. He ordered Circuit Intendant Li Xuyi to relieve the city, won a major victory, and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 十二月，复太湖，被優敘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Taihu was recovered; he received exceptional commendation in the records.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Taihu was recovered and he received special commendation.

sentences.zh: 十一年，拜文淵閣大學士，仍留總督任。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and still retained the post of governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 11 he became Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion while remaining governor-general.

sentences.zh: 時大軍圍安慶急，陳玉成、李秀成先後分兵犯湖北境，冀掣動局勢，遣將迭破之，所陷諸郡縣皆复。

translations.literal: At the time the main army was pressing the siege of Anqing urgently; Chen Yucheng and Li Xiucheng successively divided troops to invade Hubei territory, hoping to shake the overall situation; he sent generals to defeat them repeatedly, and all fallen prefectures and counties were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: While the main army pressed Anqing, Chen Yucheng and Li Xiucheng sent columns into Hubei to relieve the pressure. Guan Wen's generals defeated them repeatedly and recovered every fallen county.

sentences.zh: 八月，克安慶，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Anqing was taken; he was given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Anqing fell, and he received the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 是年，胡林翼病歿，嚴樹森代之。

translations.literal: That year, Hu Linyi died of illness and Yan Shusen replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hu Linyi died of illness and Yan Shusen succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 降捻苗沛霖踞安徽壽州，詔疆臣議剿撫之策。

translations.literal: The surrendered Nian leader Miao Peilin held Shouzhou in Anhui; an edict ordered frontier officials to deliberate policies of suppression or appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: The surrendered Nian leader Miao Peilin held Shouzhou in Anhui, and the throne ordered frontier officials to debate whether to suppress or appease him.

sentences.zh: 官文疏陳沛霖包藏禍心，罪大惡極，請伸天討。

translations.literal: Guan Wen memorialized stating that Peilin harbored treacherous designs, his crimes were extreme, and he requested that heaven's punishment be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen memorialized that Peilin harbored treasonous intent, his crimes were extreme, and heaven's punishment should fall on him.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，遣副將周鳳山等剿捻於河南信陽、羅山，敗之；

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he dispatched Deputy Commander Zhou Fengshan and others to suppress the Nian in Xinyang and Luoshan in Henan and defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1 he sent Deputy Commander Zhou Fengshan to suppress the Nian in Xinyang and Luoshan, Henan, and defeated them;

sentences.zh: 又破黃梅捻巢，收復十餘寨：晉文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: he again broke the Nian nest at Huangmei and recovered more than ten stockades: he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: then broke the Nian stronghold at Huangmei and recovered more than ten stockades. He was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 發、捻合擾楚、豫之交，勢甚熾。

translations.literal: Taiping and Nian forces jointly harassed the border of Chu and Yu; their momentum was very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping and Nian forces jointly ravaged the Hubei-Henan border with great ferocity.

sentences.zh: 荊州將軍多隆阿方督師赴陝西，官文以楚兵不敷分佈，奏調回援。

translations.literal: General of Jingzhou Duolong'a was then commanding troops on expedition to Shaanxi; Guan Wen, because Chu troops were insufficient to be distributed, memorialized to recall him for relief.
translations.idiomatic: General of Jingzhou Duolong'a was campaigning in Shaanxi; Guan Wen, finding Hubei troops too thinly spread, asked that he be recalled.

sentences.zh: 九月，多隆阿至，屢戰皆捷，襄河以北賊皆遠遁。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Duolong'a arrived; in repeated battles he was victorious, and north of the Xiang River all rebels fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Duolong'a arrived, won repeated victories, and drove all rebels north of the Xiang far away.

sentences.zh: 三年，劾巡撫嚴樹森把持剛愎，黜之。

translations.literal: In the third year, he impeached Governor Yan Shusen for domineering obstinacy and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 3 he impeached Governor Yan Shusen for domineering obstinacy and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 六月，克復江寧，曾國籓奏捷，推官文列名疏首。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Jiangning was recovered; Zeng Guofan memorialized victory and placed Guan Wen's name at the head of the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Nanjing was recovered. Zeng Guofan reported victory and placed Guan Wen's name first on the memorial.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉官文徵兵籌餉，推賢讓能，接濟東征，不分畛域，錫封一等伯爵，號果威，世襲罔替，升入正白旗滿洲，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: An edict praised Guan Wen for raising troops and securing supplies, deferring to the worthy and yielding to the able, aiding the eastern campaign without regard to territorial boundaries; he was granted a first-class earldom with the designation Guowei, hereditary without end, raised into the Manchu Plain White Banner, and given double-eyed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised Guan Wen for raising troops and funds, deferring to able colleagues, and aiding the eastern campaign without regard to boundaries. He was made a hereditary first-class earl with the designation Guowei, enrolled in the Manchu Plain White Banner, and awarded double peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 蓋褒其能與胡林翼和衷卒成大功也。

translations.literal: This was to praise his ability to work in harmony with Hu Linyi and thereby achieve great success.
translations.idiomatic: The honor reflected his harmonious cooperation with Hu Linyi in achieving victory.

sentences.zh: 四年，僧格林沁剿捻戰歿於山東，詔追論前年發、捻擾湖北，官文不能就地殲除，僅驅出境，以致蔓延益熾，下嚴議，降三級調用，改革職留任，褫宮銜、花翎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Senggelinqin was killed in battle while suppressing the Nian in Shandong; an edict reviewed the previous year when Taiping and Nian forces harassed Hubei: Guan Wen had been unable to destroy them on the spot and only drove them beyond the border, causing the disturbance to spread and grow fiercer; severe deliberation was ordered; he was demoted three ranks and transferred, changed in office but retained in post, and stripped of palace rank and peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 4 Senggelinqin was killed fighting the Nian in Shandong. The court reviewed the previous year's Taiping-Nian raids on Hubei: Guan Wen had failed to destroy them locally and merely drove them out, allowing the rebellion to spread. He was severely censured, demoted three ranks while kept in office, and stripped of palace rank and peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 五年，偕曾國籓奏設長江水師，如議行。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, together with Zeng Guofan he memorialized to establish a Yangzi naval force; it was carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 5 he and Zeng Guofan memorialized to establish a Yangzi flotilla, and the proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 湖北巡撫曾國荃劾官文貪庸驕蹇，命尚書綿森、侍郎譚廷襄往按，坐動用捐款，議革職，詔念前勞，原其尚非貪污欺罔，優與保全，解總督，仍留大學士、伯爵，罰伯俸十年。

translations.literal: Hubei Governor Zeng Guoquan impeached Guan Wen for greed, mediocrity, arrogance, and obstinacy; Ministers Miansen and Vice Minister Tan Tingxiang were ordered to investigate; he was found guilty of misusing donated funds; removal from office was deliberated; an edict, recalling his former labors and excusing him on the ground that it was not yet corruption and deceit, granted lenient preservation: he was relieved of the governorship but retained as grand secretary and earl, with earldom stipend fined for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei Governor Zeng Guoquan impeached Guan Wen for greed, incompetence, arrogance, and obstinacy. Ministers Miansen and Tan Tingxiang investigated and found misuse of donated funds. The court deliberated dismissal but, recalling his earlier service and finding no outright corruption, relieved him of the governorship while retaining his grand secretary title and earldom, with ten years' earldom stipend forfeited.

sentences.zh: 召還京，管理刑部，兼正白旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: He was recalled to the capital, directed the Ministry of Punishments, and concurrently served as commander of the Mongol Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to Beijing to direct the Ministry of Punishments and command the Mongol Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 尋出署直隸總督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he went out to serve as acting governor-general of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went out as acting governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 七年，捻匪張總愚由西路竄擾畿輔，下嚴議。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Nian rebel Zhang Zongyu raided from the western route into the capital region; severe deliberation was ordered.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 7 the Nian leader Zhang Zongyu raided the capital region from the west, and severe censure followed.

sentences.zh: 尋李鴻章、左宗棠等入援，七月，捻匪平，复宮銜、花翎。

translations.literal: Soon Li Hongzhang, Zuo Zongtang, and others came in relief; in the seventh month the Nian were pacified; his palace rank and peacock feathers were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang, Zuo Zongtang, and others soon reinforced the capital. In the seventh month the Nian were pacified, and his palace rank and peacock feathers were restored.

sentences.zh: 八年，回京，管理戶部三庫，授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he returned to the capital, directed the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue, and was appointed an imperial body minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 8 he returned to Beijing, directed the three revenue treasuries, and became an imperial body minister.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒，優詔賜卹，贈太保，賜金治喪，遣惠郡王奠醊，祀賢良祠，諡文恭。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he died; an edict of exceptional condolence was granted, he was posthumously given the title of Grand Tutor, gold was granted for the funeral, Prince Hui was sent to offer libations, he was enshrined in the Temple of Worthies, and given the posthumous name Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tongzhi 10. The court granted exceptional mourning honors, posthumously titled him Grand Tutor, funded his funeral, sent Prince Hui to offer libations, enshrined him in the Temple of Worthies, and gave him the posthumous name Wengong.

sentences.zh: 尋以疆臣請合祀湖北胡林翼專祠。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, at the request of frontier officials, he was jointly enshrined in Hu Linyi's special temple in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials soon asked that he be jointly enshrined in Hu Linyi's temple in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 當官文之在湖北，事事聽林翼所為，惟馭下不嚴，用財不節，林翼憂之。

translations.literal: When Guan Wen was in Hubei, in all matters he let Lin Yi act as he wished; only in controlling subordinates he was not strict and in spending funds he was not frugal, which Lin Yi worried about.
translations.idiomatic: While Guan Wen was in Hubei he let Hu Linyi decide everything, but his lax discipline over subordinates and lavish spending troubled Hu Linyi.

sentences.zh: 閻敬銘方佐治餉，一日林翼與言，恐誤疆事。

translations.literal: Yan Jingming was then assisting in managing supplies; one day Lin Yi spoke with him, fearing frontier affairs would be harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jingming was then managing supplies. One day Hu Linyi confided his fear that frontier affairs would suffer.

sentences.zh: 敬銘曰：「公誤矣！

translations.literal: Jingming said: "Your Excellency is mistaken!
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jingming replied: "Your Excellency is mistaken!

sentences.zh: 本朝不輕以漢大臣專兵柄。

translations.literal: Our dynasty does not lightly entrust military authority exclusively to Han grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: This dynasty does not lightly give Han ministers sole command of armies.

sentences.zh: 今滿、漢並用，而聲績炳著者多屬漢人，此聖明大公劃除畛域之效。

translations.literal: Now Manchu and Han are employed together, yet those of brilliant reputation and achievement are mostly Han; this is the effect of the sage emperor's great fairness in erasing territorial boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu and Han serve together now, yet most celebrated commanders are Han—a result of the emperor's fairness in erasing ethnic barriers.

sentences.zh: 然湖北居天下要衝，朝廷寧肯不以親信大臣臨之？

translations.literal: Yet Hubei occupies the strategic key of the realm; would the court be willing not to place a trusted intimate minister over it?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hubei is the empire's strategic pivot. Would the court fail to place a trusted intimate minister there?

sentences.zh: 夫督撫相劾，無論未必勝，即勝，能保後來者必賢耶？

translations.literal: As for governor-general and governor impeaching each other, setting aside whether you would necessarily win, even if you won, can you guarantee the successor would be worthy?
translations.idiomatic: If governor-general and governor impeach each other, you may not even win—and if you do, who guarantees a better successor?

sentences.zh: 且繼者或厲清操，勤庶務，而不明遠略，未必不顓己自是，豈甘事事讓人？

translations.literal: Moreover, a successor may be stern in personal integrity and diligent in routine affairs yet unclear in far-reaching strategy, and may not fail to be self-willed and opinionated—would he willingly yield in every matter?
translations.idiomatic: A successor might be scrupulous and diligent yet lack strategic vision, insist on his own way, and refuse to yield on everything.

sentences.zh: 官文心無成見，兼隸旗籍，每有大事，正可藉其言以伸所請。

translations.literal: Guan Wen has no fixed prejudices and is moreover of banner registration; whenever there is a major affair, you may just borrow his words to advance what you request.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen has no fixed prejudices and belongs to the banners; on major matters you can use his voice to advance your requests.

sentences.zh: 其失僅在私費奢豪，誠於事有濟，歲糜十萬金供之，未為失計。
