translations.literal: His fault lies only in private spending that is extravagant; if it truly helps affairs succeed, to spend a hundred thousand taels a year supporting him is not a mistaken plan.
translations.idiomatic: His fault is only private extravagance. If it helps the cause, spending a hundred thousand taels a year on him is no bad bargain.

sentences.zh: 至一二私人，可容，容之；

translations.literal: As for one or two private associates, if they can be tolerated, tolerate them;
translations.idiomatic: As for one or two private associates, tolerate them if you can;

sentences.zh: 不可，則以事劾去之。

translations.literal: if not, then impeach and remove them on grounds of specific matters.
translations.idiomatic: if not, impeach and remove them on specific grounds.

sentences.zh: 彼意氣素平，必無忤也。」

translations.literal: His temperament has always been even; there will certainly be no opposition."
translations.idiomatic: His temperament is even; he will not resist."

sentences.zh: 林翼大悟。

translations.literal: Lin Yi was greatly enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi was greatly enlightened.

sentences.zh: 及林翼歿，督撫不相能，官文劾嚴樹森去之；

translations.literal: When Lin Yi died, governor-general and governor could not work together; Guan Wen impeached Yan Shusen and removed him;
translations.idiomatic: After Hu Linyi died, governor-general and governor clashed. Guan Wen impeached Yan Shusen and removed him;

sentences.zh: 而曾國荃又劾官文去之。

translations.literal: and Zeng Guoquan in turn impeached Guan Wen and removed him.
translations.idiomatic: then Zeng Guoquan impeached Guan Wen and removed him in turn.

sentences.zh: 官文晚節建樹不能如曩時，然林翼非官文之虛己推誠，亦無以成大功，世故兩賢之。

translations.literal: Guan Wen's achievements in his later years could not match former times, yet without Guan Wen's emptying himself and sincere deference, Lin Yi could not have achieved great success; therefore the world esteems both as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen's later achievements did not match his early years, yet without Guan Wen's sincere deference Hu Linyi could not have succeeded; the world therefore esteems both men.

sentences.zh: 孫興恩，襲伯爵。

translations.literal: Sun Xingen inherited the earldom.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xingen inherited the earldom.

sentences.zh: 文煜，字星岩，費莫氏，滿洲正藍旗人。

translations.literal: Wen Yu, courtesy name Xingyan, of the Feimo clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yu, styled Xingyan, was a Feimo Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 由官學生授太常寺庫使，累遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: From a student of the Imperial Academy he was appointed storekeeper of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was repeatedly transferred to director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: An Imperial Academy student, he became storekeeper of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and rose to director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 出為直隸霸昌道、四川按察使。

translations.literal: He went out as Baxing circuit intendant of Zhili and provincial judicial commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Baxing circuit intendant in Zhili and judicial commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，遷江寧布政使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, he was transferred to provincial treasurer of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 he was made treasurer of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 時江寧已陷賊，文煜從琦善江北大營。

translations.literal: At the time Jiangning had already fallen to rebels; Wen Yu followed Qishan at the Great Camp north of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing had already fallen, so Wen Yu joined Qishan at the northern Yangzi camp.

sentences.zh: 四年，琦善歿於揚州，所部練勇及江北糧台事宜，命文煜接辦。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Qishan died at Yangzhou; the trained braves under his command and affairs of the grain depot north of the Yangzi were ordered to be taken over by Wen Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 4 Qishan died at Yangzhou, and Wen Yu took over his militia and the northern Yangzi grain depot.

sentences.zh: 五年春，粵匪由瓜洲東竄沙頭港，文煜遣勇擊之，賊由對岸扎簰爭渡，偕水師以大砲合擊，賊退瓜洲。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, Cantonese rebels fled east from Guazhou to Shatou Harbor; Wen Yu sent braves to attack them; the rebels on the opposite bank lashed rafts to compete in crossing; together with the navy he used great cannon in a joint attack, and the rebels withdrew to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xianfeng 5 rebels fled east from Guazhou to Shatou Harbor. Wen Yu sent militia to attack; when they lashed rafts to cross the river, he joined the navy in a cannon barrage and drove them back to Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 文煜以沙頭港為裡下河門戶，賊所必爭，築土城砲台，疏請添募練勇守禦，從之。

translations.literal: Wen Yu held that Shatou Harbor was the gateway to the Lixia River region and a place the rebels would certainly contest; he built earthen walls and batteries and memorialized to add recruitment of trained braves for defense; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yu saw Shatou Harbor as the gateway to the Lixia River region and a point the rebels would contest. He built earthen walls and batteries and asked to recruit more militia for defense; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而賊踞揚州，窺裡下河，文煜擊之於萬安橋，大有斬獲，賊勢乃挫。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels held Yangzhou and watched for a chance against the Lixia River region; Wen Yu attacked them at Wan'an Bridge with many kills and captures, and the rebel momentum was checked.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels held Yangzhou and threatened the Lixia River region, Wen Yu attacked them at Wan'an Bridge with heavy casualties on their side, checking their advance.

sentences.zh: 七年，調江蘇布政使，治江南大營糧台。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was transferred to provincial treasurer of Jiangsu and directed the grain depot of the Great Camp south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 7 he became treasurer of Jiangsu and directed the southern Yangzi army's grain depot.

sentences.zh: 以支給撙節，為軍中所不便，提督和春劾其拘泥，命來京候另簡用。

translations.literal: Because his disbursements were frugal, this was inconvenient for the army; Regional Commander He Chun impeached him for rigidity, and he was ordered to come to the capital to await another appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His frugal disbursements displeased the army. Regional Commander He Chun impeached him for rigidity, and he was ordered to Beijing to await reassignment.

sentences.zh: 尋授直隸布政使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed provincial treasurer of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed treasurer of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 九年，英兵犯大沽，為僧格林沁擊退。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, English troops attacked Dagu and were beaten back by Senggelinqin.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 9 the British attacked Dagu and were driven off by Senggelinqin.

sentences.zh: 戰後將議撫，命文煜從總督恆福赴北塘相機辦理。

translations.literal: After the battle, when appeasement was to be discussed, Wen Yu was ordered to follow Governor-General Hengfu to Beitang to handle matters as circumstances allowed.
translations.idiomatic: After the battle, as peace talks began, Wen Yu accompanied Governor-General Hengfu to Beitang to handle affairs as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 尋擢山東巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 捻匪圍曹縣，分黨擾安陵，檄曹州鎮總兵郝上庠合師內外夾擊，解曹州圍，安陵賊亦退。

translations.literal: Nian bandits besieged Caoxian and split forces to harass Anling; he ordered Caozhou garrison Regional Commander Hao Shangxiang to join armies inside and outside in a pincer attack, lifted the siege of Caozhou, and the rebels at Anling also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Nian bandits besieged Caoxian and raided Anling. He ordered Regional Commander Hao Shangxiang to attack from inside and outside, lifted the siege of Caoxian, and drove off the Anling raiders.

sentences.zh: 十年，捻匪又竄單縣，分擾嶧縣得勝徬，遣將擊走之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Nian bandits again raided into Shanxian and split forces to harass Desheng Embankment in Yixian; he sent generals and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 10 the Nian raided Shanxian and harassed Desheng Embankment in Yixian; he sent generals and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 英法聯軍踞砲台，文煜遣兵扼利津，自駐濰縣韓亭以防陸路北犯。

translations.literal: The Anglo-French allied armies held the batteries; Wen Yu sent troops to hold Lijin and himself stationed at Hanting in Weixian to guard against a land route invasion from the north.
translations.idiomatic: When the Anglo-French allies held the batteries, Wen Yu posted troops at Lijin and stationed himself at Hanting in Weixian to block a northern land advance.

sentences.zh: 尋敵船北駛犯北塘，文煜分軍入衛，駐通州，自率眾赴濟寧剿捻匪。

translations.literal: Soon enemy ships sailed north and attacked Beitang; Wen Yu divided troops to enter the capital guard, stationed at Tongzhou, and personally led forces to Jining to suppress Nian bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy ships sailed north to attack Beitang, he sent troops to defend the capital, held Tongzhou, and personally led forces to Jining against the Nian.

sentences.zh: 十一年，署直隸總督，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he served as acting governor-general of Zhili, and soon received formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 11 he acted as governor-general of Zhili and soon received formal appointment.

sentences.zh: 時和議既成，穆宗回鑾，畿輔馬賊四起，久未淨絕，屢詔責文煜搜捕。

translations.literal: At the time peace had been concluded and the Muzong Emperor returned to the capital; mounted bandits rose everywhere in the capital region and long went uncleared; edicts repeatedly rebuked Wen Yu to search and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had been made and the Tongzhi Emperor returned to Beijing, but mounted bandits plagued the capital region for years. Edicts repeatedly ordered Wen Yu to hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，坐山東降賊張錫珠等擾畿南督剿不力，褫職，戍軍台。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, because surrendered Shandong rebels Zhang Xizhu and others harassed the southern capital region and he was ineffective in supervising suppression, he was stripped of office and sent to garrison duty at the military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1 he was dismissed for failing to suppress surrendered Shandong rebels Zhang Xizhu and others who raided south of the capital, and was sent to garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 二年，僧格林沁奏調赴營差遣，尋授鑲黃旗蒙古副都統。

translations.literal: In the second year, Senggelinqin memorialized to transfer him to camp for assignment; soon afterward he was appointed vice commander of the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 2 Senggelinqin requested his transfer to camp service, and he soon became vice commander of the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 三年，命赴甘肅慶陽督辦糧台，以病請解職回旗。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was ordered to go to Qingyang in Gansu to supervise the grain depot; on grounds of illness he requested relief from office and return to his banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 3 he was ordered to supervise the grain depot at Qingyang, Gansu, but illness led him to resign and return to his banner.

sentences.zh: 七年，起授正藍旗漢軍都統，尋出為福州將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was restored and appointed commander of the Han Army of the Plain Blue Banner; soon afterward he went out as general of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 7 he was restored as commander of the Han Plain Blue Banner, then posted as general of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，兼署閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he additionally served as acting governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 10 he also served as acting governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十三年，日本兵船窺伺台灣，偕總督​​李鶴年、船政大臣疏陳防務。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Japanese warships watched for an opportunity against Taiwan; together with Governor-General Li Henian and the minister of naval administration he memorialized on coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 13 Japanese warships threatened Taiwan. With Governor-General Li Henian and the naval affairs minister he memorialized on coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，入覲，留京授內大臣、鑲白旗漢軍都統、左都御史，擢刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu, he came to audience, remained in the capital, was appointed imperial body minister, commander of the Han Army of the Bordered White Banner, and left censor-in-chief, and was promoted to minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 3 he came to audience, stayed in Beijing as imperial body minister, commander of the Han Bordered White Banner, and left censor-in-chief, and was promoted to minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 七年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he became associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 7 he became associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 九年，充總管內務府大臣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he served as supervising minister of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 9 he supervised the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜武英殿大學士，以病乞罷。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall and requested retirement on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 10 he became Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall and retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太子少保，諡文達。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; he was posthumously given the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Wenda.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was posthumously titled Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the name Wenda.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督曾國荃等奏文煜咸豐中孤軍捍賊，保全裡下河，請於揚州建專祠，允之。

translations.literal: Governor-General Zeng Guoquan of the Two Jiangs and others memorialized that in the Xianfeng era Wen Yu with an isolated army resisted rebels and preserved the Lixia River region, requesting a special temple at Yangzhou; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zeng Guoquan and others memorialized that in the Xianfeng era Wen Yu held off rebels with a lone force and saved the Lixia River region, and asked for a temple at Yangzhou; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 子志顏，理籓院侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Zhiyan was a vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhiyan served as vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 論曰：桂良以帝室葭莩，與聞軍國，數膺議和之使，無所折衝。

translations.literal: The judgment states: Gui Liang, by virtue of kinship with the imperial house through marriage, took part in military and state affairs and repeatedly received missions to negotiate peace, yet achieved no diplomatic success.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Gui Liang, as an imperial in-law, took part in military and state affairs and undertook repeated peace missions, yet achieved no diplomatic success.

sentences.zh: 瑞麟從僧格林沁勦賊防夷，曾著勞勚。

translations.literal: Rui Lin followed Senggelinqin in suppressing rebels and guarding against foreigners and once rendered notable service.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Lin campaigned with Senggelinqin against rebels and foreigners and once rendered notable service.

sentences.zh: 文煜亦處兵間，無功可錄。

translations.literal: Wen Yu also was amid warfare, yet had no achievement worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yu also saw military service but left no achievement worth recording.

sentences.zh: 官文雖無過人之才，推賢讓能，奠安江漢，與曾國籓、胡林翼和衷規畫，竟完戡定之功。

translations.literal: Guan Wen, though without surpassing talent, deferred to the worthy and yielded to the able, settled and secured the Jiang and Han regions, and with Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi planned in harmony, ultimately completing the achievement of pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen lacked surpassing talent but deferred to able men, secured the Yangzi heartland, and planned in harmony with Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi to complete the pacification.

sentences.zh: 茅土同膺，旂常並煥，豈諸人所可並語哉？

translations.literal: They alike received fiefs and enfeoffment, their banners and tablets shine together—how can the others be spoken of in the same breath?
translations.idiomatic: They alike received fiefs and enfeoffment, their honors shining together—how can the others be mentioned in the same breath?
